headline: A 2019 law requires lobbyists who have certain criminal convictions to disclose those convictions in their federal lobbying registrations and quarterly reports.
what_it_does: The law changes the federal lobbying disclosure rules. When a lobbyist is listed on a registration or quarterly report, the filing must also include the date of any conviction and a description of the offense if that lobbyist was convicted of a listed crime. The listed crimes include bribery, extortion, embezzlement, illegal kickbacks, tax evasion, fraud, conflicts of interest, false statements, perjury, and money laundering.

who_it_affects.how: Lobbyists with a qualifying conviction must have that conviction, its date, and the offense described in the registration and quarterly reports they file.

who_it_affects.group: Lobbying firms and organizations that hire lobbyists
who_it_affects.how: Firms and organizations that file lobbying reports must include the new conviction details for any listed lobbyist who has a qualifying conviction.

who_it_affects.group: The public and journalists who track lobbying
who_it_affects.how: People who read federal lobbying filings can see past convictions of listed lobbyists for the covered offenses.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 3, 2019, and the summary does not list a separate start date for the new reporting requirement.
